eea-emep-2023.note: Inventory methodology and reminder that pollutant factors are technology and control specific.

natural-gas-hhv.label: Pipeline natural gas, HHV
natural-gas-hhv.note: Pollutant values are screening estimates for commercial boilers; use measured or permit-specific factors when available.

coal-lhv.label: Coking coal, LHV screening default
coal-lhv.note: Coal composition varies widely; replace this factor for engineering or reporting work.

hydrogen.label: Hydrogen at point of use
hydrogen.note: Zero point-of-use CO2 is not zero lifecycle emissions; model production electricity or fuel separately.

SO2.name: Sulfur dioxide
SO2.category: criteria air pollutant and secondary-particle precursor
health_effects: Can irritate the respiratory system and worsen breathing symptoms, particularly for people with asthma.

NOx.name: Nitrogen oxides
health_effects: Elevated nitrogen dioxide exposure can irritate airways, aggravate asthma, and increase susceptibility to respiratory infections.
secondary_effects: contributes to acid deposition and nutrient pollution

PM2.5.name: Fine particulate matter
health_effects: Fine particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and some can enter the bloodstream, affecting respiratory and cardiovascular health.
sensitive_groups: people with heart or lung disease

PM10.name: Inhalable particulate matter
health_effects: Inhalable particles can enter the respiratory tract and aggravate respiratory conditions.

CO.name: Carbon monoxide
CO.category: criteria air pollutant and acute combustion hazard
health_effects: Carbon monoxide interferes with oxygen delivery; high exposure can cause headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, confusion, and potentially death.
sensitive_groups: people with anemia or respiratory disease

VOC.name: Volatile organic compounds
VOC.category: ozone precursor; toxicity is compound specific
health_effects: Health effects cannot be inferred from total VOC mass because toxicity varies substantially by chemical species.

NH3.name: Ammonia
health_effects: Ammonia is irritating at elevated concentrations; an emission total alone does not determine exposure.
